title: One equation, three shapes, one singular point
lede: The surface \(x^2+y^2-z^2=t\) changes shape as t moves through zero. Slide t, or press Sweep t, and watch the two sheets join into a cone and open into a single sheet.
notice: For t below 0 there are two separate sheets. At t = 0 they meet in a cone. Above 0 the surface is one connected piece.
The cone is the only singular case: the gradient of the equation vanishes at the origin, which lies on the surface only when t = 0.
For t of 0 or more the surface is covered by straight lines. The one-sheeted hyperboloid has two families of them.
hint: Drag to rotate. Slide t through zero.
